title: How to sum a column that contains errors
task: Get a total even when some cells are #N/A or #DIV/0! — without cleaning the data first.

excel.note: Function 9 = SUM, option 6 = ignore errors. Excel/LibreOffice; not in Google Sheets.

google_sheets.note: Sheets has no AGGREGATE. This handles #N/A; for all error types use =SUM(IFERROR(A2:A6,0)) entered as an array.

explanation: A plain SUM propagates any error — one #DIV/0! in the range makes the whole total an error. AGGREGATE(9,6,range) sums (function code 9) while ignoring errors (option 6), so the two good-plus-good rows total 10+20+30 = 60 despite the #DIV/0! and #N/A in between. AGGREGATE lives in Excel and LibreOffice but NOT Google Sheets — there, wrap the values in IFERROR (=SUM(IFERROR(A2:A6,0)) entered with Ctrl+Shift+Enter in older versions, or it just spills in modern ones), or SUMIF around specific error types. The same AGGREGATE trick does error-ignoring AVERAGE (code 1), MAX (4), COUNT (2) and more.
